why: Cd2 is the mouse ortholog of human CD2 and encodes CD2 (LFA-2, T11), an immunoglobulin-superfamily adhesion receptor on T cells and natural killer cells. CD2 binds CD58 (or CD48 in mice) and has been associated with cell adhesion and costimulation of T-cell activation.
CD2 is a target of agents used in psoriasis and transplantation and has been studied in T-cell-directed therapy. Cd2-deficient mice are viable with altered T-cell responses in some settings.
applications: Humanized CD2 models, in which the human protein replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate CD2-directed agents in defined experimental settings.

why: Ccr6 is the mouse ortholog of human CCR6 and encodes CCR6 (CD196), a class A G-protein-coupled chemokine receptor that binds CCL20. CCR6 is expressed on Th17 cells, regulatory T cells, and other leukocytes and has been associated with their recruitment to mucosal and inflamed tissues.

CCR6 has been associated with psoriasis, inflammatory bowel disease, and tumor immunity, and CCR6-pathway-directed approaches are under study. Ccr6-deficient mice show altered mucosal immune responses.
applications: Humanized CCR6 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate CCR6-directed agents in defined experimental settings.

why: Cxcr6 is the mouse ortholog of human CXCR6 and encodes CXCR6 (CD186), a class A G-protein-coupled chemokine receptor that binds CXCL16. CXCR6 has been associated with the positioning and retention of tissue-resident and other T cells.
CXCR6 has been associated with antitumor immunity, liver disease, and inflammation, and the CXCL16-CXCR6 axis is under study. Cxcr6-deficient mice show altered tissue-resident T-cell populations.

why: Il12b is the mouse ortholog of human IL12B and encodes the p40 subunit shared by interleukin-12 and interleukin-23. The p40 subunit pairs with p35 to form IL-12 and with p19 to form IL-23, cytokines that have been associated with Th1 and Th17 responses.
The shared p40 subunit is targeted by antibodies used in psoriasis and inflammatory bowel disease. Il12b-deficient mice show impaired IL-12- and IL-23-dependent responses.
applications: Humanized IL12B models, in which the human subunit replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate p40-directed biologics in defined experimental settings.

why: Cd46 is the mouse ortholog of human CD46 and encodes membrane cofactor protein (MCP), a complement-regulatory protein that acts as a cofactor for inactivation of complement components C3b and C4b. CD46 has been associated with protection of host cells from complement.

CD46 serves as a receptor for certain measles virus strains and other pathogens and has been associated with roles in cancer, and CD46-directed approaches are under study. In mice, Cd46 is expressed mainly in the testis, unlike the broad expression of human CD46.
applications: Humanized CD46 models, which express human CD46, have been used to study CD46 biology, including as a viral receptor, and to evaluate CD46-directed approaches in defined experimental settings.

why: Angpt2 is the mouse ortholog of human ANGPT2 and encodes angiopoietin-2, a secreted ligand of the endothelial receptor Tie2. Angiopoietin-2 has been associated with context-dependent regulation of blood-vessel stability and angiogenesis.

Angiopoietin-2 has been associated with tumor angiogenesis, retinal vascular disease, and vascular leak, and ANGPT2-directed approaches, including in combination with VEGF inhibition, are in use or under study. Angpt2-deficient mice show lymphatic and vascular defects.
applications: Humanized ANGPT2 models, in which the human protein replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate angiopoietin-2-directed agents in defined experimental settings.

why: AGTR1 (mouse ortholog Agtr1a, with a related Agtr1b) encodes the angiotensin II type 1 receptor (AT1), a class A G-protein-coupled receptor. AT1 signaling in response to angiotensin II has been associated with vasoconstriction and regulation of blood pressure and fluid balance.

The AT1 receptor is the target of angiotensin-receptor blockers used widely in hypertension and cardiovascular and kidney disease. Mice lacking AT1 receptors show low blood pressure and kidney changes.
applications: Humanized AGTR1 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate AT1-receptor-directed agents in defined experimental settings.

why: Asgr1 is the mouse ortholog of human ASGR1 and encodes the major subunit of the asialoglycoprotein receptor, a C-type lectin on hepatocytes that binds galactose- and N-acetylgalactosamine-terminated glycoproteins and mediates their uptake. ASGR1 has been associated with clearance of desialylated glycoproteins.

ASGR1 is used for liver-targeted drug delivery (for example, GalNAc-conjugated therapeutics), and loss-of-function ASGR1 variants have been associated with lower non-HDL cholesterol and cardiovascular risk. Asgr1-deficient mice show altered glycoprotein clearance.
applications: Humanized ASGR1 models, in which the human receptor replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to evaluate ASGR1-targeted delivery and agents in defined experimental settings.

why: Alb is the mouse ortholog of human ALB and encodes serum albumin, the most abundant protein in blood plasma, produced by the liver. Albumin has been associated with maintenance of plasma oncotic pressure and with transport of many endogenous and exogenous molecules.

Albumin’s long circulating half-life is used in drug design to extend the half-life of therapeutics, and albumin is used clinically as a volume expander. Alb-deficient mice are viable with altered plasma protein handling.
applications: Humanized ALB models, in which the human protein replaces the mouse counterpart, have been used to study the pharmacokinetics of albumin-binding and albumin-fused therapeutics in defined experimental settings.

why: HBA1 encodes an alpha-globin subunit of adult hemoglobin; in mice the orthologous alpha-globin genes include Hba-a1 and Hba-a2. Alpha-globin combines with beta-globin and heme to form hemoglobin, which has been associated with oxygen transport in red blood cells.

Deletions and mutations affecting the alpha-globin genes cause alpha-thalassemia, and the alpha-globin locus is studied in hematology and gene-therapy research. Mouse models carrying human alpha-globin alleles have been developed to study these conditions.
applications: Humanized HBA1 models, including those carrying human alpha-globin alleles, have been used to study alpha-globin disorders in defined experimental settings.

why: Mecp2 is the mouse ortholog of human MECP2 and encodes methyl-CpG-binding protein 2, a transcriptional regulator that binds methylated DNA and is highly expressed in neurons. MeCP2 has been associated with regulation of gene expression in the nervous system.

MECP2 mutations cause Rett syndrome, and duplication of the gene causes MECP2 duplication syndrome; MECP2-directed gene therapies are under study. Mecp2-deficient and mutant mice reproduce many features of Rett syndrome.
applications: Humanized MECP2 models, including those carrying disease-associated alleles, have been used to study MeCP2 biology and Rett syndrome and to evaluate MECP2-directed approaches in defined experimental settings.
